patch_description: The original program just placed 14 random points, giving a terrible min/max distance ratio. Instead, I use a two-phase approach inspired by known spherical codes: (1) initialize with a well-spread configuration on the unit sphere (icosphere-like plus optimized placement), then (2) run a repulsion-based optimization where all pairwise distances are pushed toward the maximum distance using a soft-min "log-sum-exp" penalty on small distances. This effectively performs simulated-annealing-style gradient descent on the min/max ratio objective directly. Points are normalized to the unit sphere each step (scaling-invariant objective makes this a safe constraint), with the final configuration rescaled so the maximum distance equals a fixed value. This is a fundamentally different approach from random placement: it directly optimizes the target metric with gradient-based continuous optimization and multiple random restarts with fixed seeds for reproducibility.
